items.title: Burkina/Santé : Ouagadougou accueille la 2e édition du SIPSIS sous le signe de la souveraineté sanitaire
items.description: Le comité d'organisation de la deuxième édition du Salon international des professionnels de santé et de l'intégration des soins (SIPSIS) a dévoilé, ce vendredi 6 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, le programme de l'événement, prévu du 25 au 28 novembre 2026 au Centre international de conférences de Ouaga 2000. Placée sous le thème « Défis sanitaires de la décennie 2027-2036 en Afrique : perspectives stratégiques pour la confédération de l'Alliance des États du Sahel dans le contexte de la souveraineté », cette deuxième édition aura pour pays invités spéciaux le Mali et le Niger. Selon les organisateurs, l'objectif général du SIPSIS 2026 est de contribuer à la souveraineté sanitaire de la confédération de l'Alliance des États du Sahel et de l'Afrique, à travers une mobilisation coordonnée de l'écosystème de la santé. Cette rencontre sera l'occasion de réfléchir aux priorités sanitaires de la décennie 2027-2036 et de faire émerger des projets et des partenariats susceptibles de renforcer les capacités locales et la synergie d'action entre les différents acteurs du secteur. Le programme de cette deuxième édition sera ponctué d'activités scientifiques, d'expositions, de rencontres B2B, de visites du centre hospitalier universitaire de Pala et du barrage de Samendeni, ainsi que de la Nuit de l'écosystème de santé. « Pour le Burkina Faso, les retombées attendues concernent la valorisation des capacités nationales des différents maillons de notre écosystème sanitaire. L'accueil des délégations pourrait également soutenir le secteur économique. "SIPSIS et jeunesse" et le manuel des métiers doivent susciter des vocations et préparer une relève consciente de la diversité au sein de l'écosystème et des enjeux de la souveraineté sanitaire », a souligné le directeur de cabinet du ministère de la Santé, le Dr Adjima Combary. Dr Adjima Combary, directeur de cabinet du ministère de la Santé. Il a également précisé qu'à l'échelle de la confédération de l'Alliance des États du Sahel, le SIPSIS 2026 devrait permettre d'identifier des priorités communes et des complémentarités. Les échanges devraient ainsi favoriser l'émergence de projets conjoints, le développement de coopérations en matière de production et d'approvisionnement, ainsi qu'une meilleure coordination face aux défis sanitaires. Pour l'Afrique, le directeur de cabinet du ministère de la Santé a indiqué que les résultats attendus portent notamment sur une meilleure circulation des connaissances, une plus grande visibilité des innovations et des savoirs thérapeutiques africains, ainsi que le renforcement des coopérations entre institutions, entreprises et chercheurs. « J'appelle donc les départements ministériels, les institutions, les professionnels, les entreprises et les organisations de l'écosystème à identifier une contribution concrète, selon leurs missions et leurs capacités dans le sillage des objectifs du SIPSIS », a-t-il lancé. Pour rappel, la deuxième édition du SIPSIS se tiendra du 25 au 28 novembre 2026 au Centre international de conférences de Ouaga 2000, à Ouagadougou. Elle est placée sous le patronage du président du Faso et président de la Confédération de l'Alliance des États du Sahel, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. L'événement se déroulera également sous la présidence de Basolma Bazié, président de la Commission nationale de la Confédération de l'Alliance des États du Sahel. Jean Élysée Nikiéma Lefaso.net

items.title: Obuasi SHTS headmaster has not been cleared of sexual abuse allegations – GES
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has clarified that the Headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Abdulai Zakaria, has not been cleared of allegations of sexual abuse involving female students. The Service says its Disciplinary Committee is still investigating the matter and has not completed its work, contrary to reports suggesting that the headmaster had been exonerated. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Friday, November 6, the Public Relations Officer of the GES, Daniel Fenyi, said no individual involved in the matter had been cleared. “The issue is very sensitive. The best we can do to serve our stakeholders is to give them up-to-speed accurate information regarding what’s happening. First of all, no single individual in this whole matter has been cleared. “The headmaster has not been cleared. In fact, just as you mentioned, the committee is yet to finalise its work,” he stated. Mr Fenyi was responding to questions about the status of investigations into the allegations, following reports suggesting that the committee had completed its work and cleared the headmaster. He explained that the committee, which was initially expected to submit its findings on Wednesday, had requested additional time to engage all the alleged victims before concluding its investigations. According to him, the committee considers the accounts of the affected students essential to producing a comprehensive report that reflects their experiences. He said some of the students who had been scheduled to meet the committee did not honour their appointments, while others required alternative arrangements to participate in the process. Mr Fenyi said the GES management had consequently granted the committee an additional seven working days to complete its engagements and gather the necessary information. “The reason is quite simple: they wish that, by the time they are done, the report will reflect the genuine experiences of all the participants or victims in the whole saga. Management thought that no, this is very genuine. “If you want a seven-working-day extension to be able to reach every single individual, then that is sound. And so, management granted.” The GES spokesperson assured stakeholders that the investigation remained ongoing and that the Service expected the committee to complete its work within the extended period. He said the committee had also visited the Obuasi SHTS campus to interact with students and gather further information to support its investigations.

items.title: Police arrest four over murder of 50-year-old man in Nasarawa
items.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Police Command has arrested four suspects in connection with the alleged murder of a 50-year-old man, Jude Thaddeus, popularly known as Musa, whose decomposed remains were recovered from a dry well at his residence in Aku Village, Base 5, Karu Local Government Area of the state. The remains were discovered after the victim’s sister, identified as 46-year-old Jenifer Alain, reported his disappearance to the police on November 1, 2026. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Ramhan Nansel, disclosed this to journalists in Lafia, saying the complainant had become concerned after repeated attempts to reach her brother failed, with unidentified persons answering his telephone calls. According to Nansel, detectives attached to the division launched an investigation following the complaint, leading to the arrest of a 23-year-old suspect, Yusuf Musa. He said preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect had been employed by the deceased about three months earlier to look after his domestic animals and had subsequently been introduced to neighbours and other members of the community. The police spokesman said further findings indicated that the deceased had been missing since October 22, while the suspect allegedly took possession of his mobile phone and deceived callers by claiming that his supposed father had travelled to England. He added that investigations also revealed that the suspect had allegedly been disposing of the deceased’s personal belongings, domestic animals and other property under suspicious circumstances. Nansel said the suspect reportedly confessed to selling some heavy metals and industrial engines belonging to the deceased for N3.4 million. “During interrogation, Yusuf Musa allegedly confessed to his involvement in the killing of Jude Thaddeus and disclosed that the victim’s body had been dumped in a dry well within his residence,” he said. Following the disclosure, a team of detectives, assisted by environmental health personnel, visited the scene and evacuated the decomposed remains from the well. The police said preliminary findings suggested that the victim was allegedly killed inside his residence before his body was dumped in the well and set ablaze. The suspects were also alleged to have used several blocks to seal and conceal the well in an attempt to cover up the crime and evade detection. The remains were subsequently taken to the Medical Centre, Mararaba, where a medical doctor examined and certified the victim dead. Nansel said further investigations led to the arrest of three additional suspects, including persons allegedly found with some of the deceased’s stolen belongings. He disclosed that one other suspect had been identified but remained at large, adding that efforts were ongoing to apprehend the fleeing suspect and establish the roles of all those connected with the incident. The Commissioner of Police, Nasarawa State Command, CP Shetima Jauro Mohamed, has directed that the case be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Lafia, for comprehensive investigation and diligent prosecution of those found culpable. The commissioner commended the detectives for their prompt response and professionalism in uncovering the circumstances surrounding the victim’s disappearance and the recovery of his remains. He reiterated the command’s commitment to apprehending perpetrators of crime and urged residents to report suspicious movements and activities to the nearest police station. The post Police arrest four over murder of 50-year-old man in Nasarawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Apprise Music takes Ghanaian artists to WOMEX 2026 in Spain
items.description: Ghanaian music company Apprise Music & Media has completed its fourth participation in the Worldwide Music Expo, with its latest attendance highlighting efforts to expand international opportunities for Ghanaian musicians and strengthen connections between Africa’s music sector and the global live music industry. Held from October 21 to 25, 2026, in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain, WOMEX brought together music professionals, festival organisers, booking agents, record labels, publishers, cultural institutions and performing artists from across international markets. The annual gathering combines a trade fair, professional conferences, networking activities and live music showcases, with programming spanning traditional, folk, roots, jazz, contemporary and diaspora music. Apprise Music was represented by its Founder and Chief Executive Officer, Michael Kwabena Bamfo, and Chief Operating Officer and Head of Publishing, Grace Nyele Mensah. Their participation centred on introducing Ghanaian artists to international music professionals, developing relationships with cultural and commercial organisations, and examining the challenges affecting African musicians seeking sustainable careers beyond their domestic markets. During the five-day gathering, the Apprise Music delegation held discussions with representatives from international music organisations, record labels, festival networks and cultural institutions. Among the engagements reported by the company were meetings with a representative of the Recording Academy, the organisation behind the Grammy Awards, and a vice president of The Orchard, the music distribution and artist services company owned by Sony Music Entertainment. The delegation also connected with cultural activists, festival promoters, artist managers, music entrepreneurs and professionals involved in international touring and artistic exchange. The meetings covered areas of potential cooperation including international market access, artist development, live performance opportunities, music rights administration and cross-border cultural projects. Apprise Music has not announced formal agreements arising from these meetings, and the discussions should not be interpreted as confirmed partnerships with the Recording Academy, The Orchard or other participating organisations. A central part of the company’s participation was the presentation of Ghanaian music projects to international booking agents, festival programmers, promoters and other professionals involved in discovering and developing artists. The pitching activities included music and promotional materials associated with Epixode, Abiana, Yinewin, King Nzema, King Eazie, Ayizam and Rama Black, alongside other performers. The selection reflected an interest in presenting different aspects of Ghana’s contemporary musical expression, including artists whose work incorporates live instrumentation, local languages, traditional influences and modern production. The initiative sought to expand the professional networks available to these musicians and identify international markets where their recordings and live performances could attract further interest. Although music streaming platforms have made African recordings increasingly accessible to international listeners, access to overseas concert stages often depends on additional industry structures, including booking agents, touring representatives, festival networks, cultural institutions and professional management. Beyond commercial opportunities, Apprise Music’s involvement at WOMEX also reflected a broader interest in the international representation of Ghana’s musical heritage, including Highlife, indigenous percussion, regional folk traditions and local-language compositions. The company is also interested in the role of music in cultural diplomacy, particularly how artistic exchanges can develop relationships between African musicians and international communities. Apprise Music & Media was founded in Ghana in 2018 and operates in digital music distribution, publishing administration, rights management and music business education. Following WOMEX 2026, the company intends to continue discussions with contacts made during the gathering and assess opportunities for future artist showcases, touring arrangements, music education and cultural exchange programmes.

items.title: 2027: Obi couldn’t confront Anambra’s erosion, he lacks leadership traits — Tinubu
items.description: President Bola Tinubu has criticised the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, over his handling of erosion in Anambra State, questioning his leadership qualities ahead of the 2027 general election. Tinubu spoke on Friday at the All Progressives Congress rally held at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, where he urged voters not to support Obi in the forthcoming presidential election. The President compared Obi’s record in Anambra with his own efforts to address coastal challenges in Lagos and those of Akwa Ibom Governor Umo Eno. “He’s in one party, they called NDC, who is running for President; he ran away from erosion in Anambra State. He could not confront erosion,” Tinubu said. “I, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, I confronted the Atlantic Ocean, I tamed it for you. Umo Eno confronted the erosion in Akwa Ibom, and it’s working for you.” The President argued that Obi lacked the leadership qualities required to govern the country, citing his departure from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and subsequent move to the NDC. “They lack leadership character and traits,” Tinubu said. He questioned Obi’s decision to leave the PDP after previously being associated with the party, describing the move as evidence of a lack of political leadership. “If a man that once upon a time was a baby of PDP became a father of PDP and because of a little inconvenience he ran away from that party and formed a dangerous aide-de-camp in another party, is that a leadership trait? Is that a leadership character?” he asked. Tinubu further challenged Obi’s presidential ambition, telling supporters that the former Anambra governor was not fit to lead the country. “And he wants you to vote for him; it’s not for banana. He cannot put a house in order,” the President said. The rally formed part of Tinubu’s visit to Akwa Ibom, where he inaugurated projects executed by the Eno administration before attending the APC political gathering. items.title: NDLEA remands two Mexicans, four Nigerians over Oyo meth lab
items.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arraigned two Mexican nationals and four Nigerians over their alleged involvement in the establishment and operation of a clandestine methamphetamine laboratory in Tapa village, Ibarapa North Local Government Area of Oyo State. The six defendants were arraigned before Justice Nkeonye Evelyn Maha of the Federal High Court, Ibadan, on a four-count charge bordering on conspiracy, drug trafficking and the illegal production of methamphetamine. The NDLEA Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement on Friday. The defendants are 56-year-old Mexican, Jose Villa Ochoa; another Mexican, Carrera Loaiza Arturo, 40; and four Nigerians identified as Maxwell Uche Nevoh, 30; Olatunji Yusuf, 37; Bankole Akeem Owolabi, 45; and Ganiu Monsiu, 43. According to the statement, NDLEA operatives arrested Ochoa and the four Nigerian defendants on June 17, 2026, in a forested area of Tapa village, while Arturo was arrested on August 19, 2026, at the Lagos airport while allegedly attempting to flee the country. Babafemi said the four-count charge accused the defendants of conspiring to operate a drug trafficking organisation and establishing a clandestine laboratory for the production of methamphetamine between December 2025 and June 2026 at different locations in Lagos and Oyo states. They were also accused of unlawfully transporting and distributing chemical substances intended for the manufacture of methamphetamine, contrary to Section 20(1)(f) and punishable under Section 20(2)(a) of the NDLEA Act. All six defendants pleaded not guilty when the charges were read to them. Following their pleas, Justice Maha ordered that they be remanded at the Correctional Centre in Ibadan. The case was adjourned until January 26, 27, 28 and 29, 2027, for trial. The NDLEA spokesman also disclosed that three other Mexican nationals and seven Nigerians arrested over a similar alleged operation at a forest hideout in Ogun State on May 16, 2026, had been remanded following their arraignment before a Federal High Court in Lagos. He said the court had rejected their bail application and ordered an accelerated hearing of the case. items.title: L’Égypte réclame la restitution des restes du prêtre Nakht, conservés dans un musée de Glasgow
items.description: Les autorites egyptiennes ont demande la restitution des restes du pretre Nakht, vieux de pres de 4 000 ans et conserves au musee et galerie d'art Kelvingrove de Glasgow, en ecosse. Leur retrait de l'exposition publique, fin octobre, pour des raisons ethiques, avait suscite un debat dans le pays. La direction du musee avait decide de soustraire ces restes au regard des visiteurs en raison de l'absence de « consentement du defunt » ou de ses descendants, rapportent les medias locaux. Cette decision s'inscrit dans une reflexion sur les pratiques museales, nourrie par la revision du Code de deontologie du Conseil international des musees (ICOM), qui recommande de respecter la « dignite inherente » des restes humains, sans imposer pour autant leur retrait systematique des expositions. Le ministre egyptien du Tourisme et des Antiquites, Sherif Fathy, a confirme a l'agence americaine Bloomberg que son pays avait demande le rapatriement des restes de Nakht. « Nous sommes actuellement en train de communiquer et de prendre les mesures necessaires », a-t-il declare, avant d'ajouter : « Nous verrons comment les choses evoluent, car de telles questions ne sont pas simples. » Il ne s'agit pas d'une momie intacte Le catalogue officiel du musee retient l'orthographe « Nakht », tandis que la plupart des articles de presse utilisent « Nekht ». Le cercueil peint qui abrite ses restes porte des inscriptions identifiant le defunt comme un pretre, alors meme que ses dimensions indiquent qu'il avait initialement ete concu pour un enfant. Le musee explique cette particularite par la decomposition probable de la momie originelle de Nakht, dont les restes auraient ensuite ete reinhumes dans ce cercueil. Il s'agit donc du squelette d'un homme adulte, et non d'une momie intacte, ce qui rend l'expression « restes d'un ancien pretre egyptien » plus adequate. Le sarcophage a ete decouvert par l'archeologue John Garstang dans une tombe de Beni Hasan, en Moyenne-egypte. Datant de la XIIe dynastie, soit approximativement de 1985 a 1797 avant J.-C., il a ete « donne » a la ville de Glasgow en 1923. Les vestiges et les artefacts de l'egypte pharaonique constituent aujourd'hui un attrait majeur pour les touristes du monde entier. Depuis plusieurs annees, les autorites egyptiennes reclament le rapatriement d'objets antiques emportes notamment en Europe et aux etats-Unis, durant l'ere coloniale. Le pays a d'ailleurs inaugure en 2025 le Grand Musee egyptien, un edifice aux dimensions et au coût litteralement pharaoniques, destine a conserver et a exposer certains des tresors les plus emblematiques de l'egypte antique.

items.title: CBN sets N10bn, N15bn capital requirements for stablecoin issuers
items.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has introduced new regulatory guidelines for stablecoin issuers and other virtual asset service providers, setting minimum paid-up capital requirements of N10 billion and N15 billion for two categories of operators. The requirements are contained in a circular dated November 5, 2026, with reference number PSP/DIR/PUB/CIR/001/004, signed by the Director of Payments Systems Policy, Musa Jimoh. Under the new guidelines, Class 1 licensed issuers, covering naira-referenced stablecoins, are required to maintain a minimum paid-up capital of N10 billion, while Class 2 issuers, covering foreign currency-referenced stablecoins, must maintain N15 billion. The bank said the capital requirements must be maintained at entry and throughout the period of operation, adding that it reserves the right to prescribe higher amounts. It also ruled out exemptions for offshore issuers, stating that all operators must comply with Nigerian incorporation, licensing and capital requirements. “Both classes shall comply with the capital deposit and corresponding evidence and supplementary requirements in Section 17. There is no offshore issuer exemption from incorporation, licensing or capital,” the circular stated. The CBN explained that Class 1 stablecoins are digital tokens designed to maintain a stable value against the naira, while Class 2 stablecoins are pegged to foreign currencies, including the US dollar. The apex bank said the growing use of virtual assets, stablecoins and tokenised payment instruments presented opportunities for innovation in payments, remittances, settlements and digital commerce. It, however, warned that their increasing adoption also posed risks to financial stability, monetary policy, consumer protection, foreign exchange management and efforts to combat illicit financial activities. According to the bank, the guidelines establish a risk-based framework for licensing, regulating, supervising and overseeing non-security virtual assets, including stablecoins, Deposit Money Tokens (DMTs) and related Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs). It said the framework was designed to support responsible innovation while safeguarding the integrity, stability and efficiency of Nigeria’s financial system. The guidelines also prescribe requirements covering corporate governance, prudential standards, consumer protection, operational resilience, anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing, as well as reporting obligations. On peer-to-peer (P2P) transactions, the CBN directed virtual asset providers to establish criteria for identifying customers who buy, sell or exchange regulated tokens as a business. The criteria, which must be approved by the providers’ boards and communicated to the CBN, are expected to consider transaction volumes, frequency, number of counterparties and advertisement of exchange rates. The bank further directed providers to apply enhanced due diligence and transaction limits to such customers and report them to the regulator. It warned that identifying a customer as a business operator would not automatically authorise the person to conduct regulated activities. Such customers, it said, must obtain the appropriate licence or authorisation, cease the activity or operate as agents of licensed providers, as directed by the bank. The CBN said the regulations were also intended to preserve the effectiveness of monetary policy instruments and strengthen its capacity to monitor capital flows and foreign exchange movements. Other objectives include protecting consumers against issuer insolvency, mismanagement of reserves or backing assets, denial of redemption, fraud and other risks. The guidelines apply to naira-referenced stablecoins, foreign currency-referenced stablecoins, Deposit Money Tokens and other designated tokens that fall within the CBN’s regulatory mandate over payments, settlements, foreign exchange, banking and financial stability. items.title: FG targets 2,000 new CNG facilities nationwide
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Federal Government has announced plans to deploy about 2,000 additional Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) infrastructure units across the country to accelerate adoption of the alternative fuel and reduce transportation costs. Executive Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (PI-CNG/EV), Ismaeel Ahmed, disclosed this on Friday shortly after the commissioning of a Rolling Energy CNG refuelling station for the State House in Karu, Abuja. Ahmed said Nigeria currently had about 160 operational CNG refuelling stations, while another 170 were at various stages of development or awaiting approval from the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). He said the programme had moved beyond the proof-of-concept stage, with private investors committing about $2.6 billion to the development of CNG infrastructure. According to him, President Bola Tinubu has directed a fresh round of infrastructure expansion involving 1,500 units in February and another 500 in August through the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF). He said the additional facilities were expected to become operational between this year and early next year. “This is almost our 106th station across the country in less than two years. This is not beginning any longer. The market has been proven,” Ahmed said. He noted that Nigeria, with an estimated population of 220 million and about 12 million vehicles, needed to accelerate the deployment of refuelling facilities to meet growing demand. On the impact of CNG adoption on transportation costs, Ahmed said fares had dropped by between 30 and 40 per cent on routes where CNG-powered buses operate. He cited the Kano-Katsina route, where passengers who previously paid between N3,000 and N4,000 could now travel for about N1,500 using CNG-powered buses. “It has significantly reduced about 30 to 40 per cent of transportation fees in the routes where CNG buses are ferrying,” he said. The PI-CNG/EV chairman, however, acknowledged that existing facilities were inadequate to meet national demand, adding that the government was working to extend CNG-powered transportation to more commercial routes and underserved communities. Also speaking, the Permanent Secretary, State House, Temitope Peter Fashedemi, said the commissioning of the facility demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to leading by example in adopting CNG as an alternative to petrol. He said the initiative had become particularly important following the removal of petrol subsidy, which increased transportation costs and made cheaper alternative fuels imperative. Fashedemi explained that the State House partnered with Rolling Energy to rehabilitate an abandoned petrol station in Karu and convert it into a CNG refuelling and vehicle conversion facility. He said the State House provided the facility, while the private sector partner handled its rehabilitation and installation without any financial contribution from the government. “State House hasn’t spent any naira in this place, but we made this place available for this purpose and they have renovated it to the extent that you have seen,” he said. He disclosed that about 10 recently acquired JAC vehicles in the State House were hybrid vehicles, while some buses used for shuttle services within the Presidential Villa also operated on hybrid technology. According to him, arrangements were underway for interested State House staff to convert eligible vehicles to CNG-powered hybrid vehicles in the coming weeks. In his remarks, the Chief Executive Officer of Rolling Energy, Mubarak Danbatta, said the newly commissioned facility was an integrated CNG refuelling station capable of dispensing gas to about 150 vehicles daily, depending on cylinder capacity and pressure. He added that its vehicle conversion centre could handle approximately 12 vehicles daily. Danbatta described the project as an example of an effective public-private partnership, noting that the State House provided the abandoned facility while Rolling Energy undertook its rehabilitation and installation. He said the company currently operated facilities in Ilorin and Abuja and was preparing to commission two additional stations in Kano and two in Kaduna. “We are targeting that by the end of the year, we will have close to 15 facilities nationwide,” he said. items.title: World Bank, IMF recognise Tinubu’s economic reforms – $1tn economy target achievable – Yilwatda
items.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, has said Nigeria’s ambition of building a $1 trillion economy is within reach, citing the economic reforms introduced by President Bola Tinubu and their recognition by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF). Yilwatda said the reforms were laying the foundation for a stronger, more productive and prosperous economy, adding that abandoning them would reverse the progress made in addressing the country’s longstanding structural challenges. He stated this in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, where President Tinubu and his entourage attended a rally at the Senator Godswill Akpabio International Stadium. In a statement issued on Friday by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, the APC chairman said Tinubu’s decision to confront longstanding economic challenges demonstrated the kind of leadership required to reposition the country for sustainable growth. Although he acknowledged that the reforms had imposed difficult adjustments on Nigerians, Yilwatda argued that sustaining them was necessary to achieve long-term economic stability. He described the $1 trillion economy target as more than a political aspiration, saying it was a national development objective supported by deliberate policy choices and ongoing economic restructuring. Yilwatda identified investments in infrastructure, transportation, education, maritime development and financial inclusion as key pillars of the administration’s economic agenda. He specifically highlighted the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, saying the project would improve connectivity, stimulate commercial activities and create economic opportunities for Akwa Ibom and other coastal communities. The APC chairman also said the administration’s focus on developing the maritime sector would enhance the competitiveness of coastal states and increase their contribution to national development. On education and social investment, he commended the student loan scheme for expanding access to higher education, while noting that interventions targeting women and small businesses were creating opportunities for wider economic participation. He further said the tax reforms were designed to reduce the burden on low-income earners and small businesses, allowing them to retain more of their earnings and operate in a more favourable business environment. Yilwatda also listed improved industrial harmony in educational institutions and efforts to settle outstanding obligations to workers, pensioners and retirees of formerly privatised public enterprises as achievements of the administration. Urging Nigerians to support the reform process, he said: “Never again should Nigeria return to Egypt. We cannot afford to abandon the difficult but necessary work of rebuilding our economy and repositioning our country for sustainable growth.” He maintained that the administration’s policies and investments were positioning Nigeria for long-term prosperity and greater economic competitiveness. items.title: Kenya : 200 ans de prison pour le gourou d’une secte qui affamait ses fidèles pour « rencontrer Jésus »
items.description: Screenshot " data-large-file="https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/IMG_1313.jpeg?fit=1024%2C687&ssl=1" /> Le gourou d'une secte évangélique apocalyptique, jugé coupable du meurtre de 190 enfants et d'un adulte après avoir encouragé ses disciples à mourir de faim pour « rencontrer Jésus », a été condamné vendredi à 200 ans de prison. Des centaines de corps avaient été découverts en 2023 dans l'arrière-pays près des plages de Malindi, sur la côté kényane dans un drame rapidement nommé le « massacre de la forêt de Shakahola » par les médias kényans, une des pires tragédies liées à des dérives sectaires qui a traumatisé le pays d'Afrique de l'Est. Le mois dernier, le tribunal de la ville portuaire de Mombasa, au bord de l'océan Indien, a jugé le pasteur autoproclamé et ancien chauffeur de taxi Paul Mackenzie, ainsi que 28 complices, coupables des meurtres de 190 enfants et d'un adulte entre janvier 2021 et septembre 2023. M. Mackenzie, portant un polo gris, est resté impassible au prononcé de sa sentence : 200 ans d’emprisonnement. Plusieurs de ses 28 coaccusés avaient affamé leurs propres enfants, empêché que d'autres fidèles ne s'enfuient, et creusé les tombes des défunts. La plupart des accusés n'ont montré ensuite aucun remord. Vingt-six ont été condamnés à des peines comprises entre 100 et 160 années de prison et deux ont écopé de 10 ans d’emprisonnement. Le parquet avait réclamé en début de semaine la peine capitale pour le gourou, une disposition inscrite dans la loi kényane, mais qui n'a plus été exécutée depuis 1987. Alors que, selon les survivants, « à Shakahola, la mort était célébrée comme un mariage avec Jésus (…) une peine de mort pourrait ne pas être vécue comme une sanction, mais comme un triomphe et une forme de martyre », a déclaré la juge Diana Kavedza Mochache pour justifier son recours à des peines de prison. « Des enfants ont vu leurs frères et sœurs mourir sous leurs yeux, (…) ont été battus, ont enduré une agonie atroce pendant que leurs parents mangeaient et buvaient. Certains sont morts par strangulation. D'autres, sévèrement battus », a poursuivi la magistrate, pour qui M. Mackenzie avait transformé la confiance de ses fidèles en « une arme de contrôle total ». « Aucune sentence ne peut apaiser la douleur que je ressens après avoir perdu les miens », a réagi auprès de l'AFP Francis Wanje, un enseignant à la retraite de 62 ans dont la fille, le gendre et deux petits-enfants ont péri dans la tragédie. – « Hiérarchie de la mort » – Un autre de ses petits-fils, 11 ans aujourd'hui, avait selon des documents judiciaires jeûné pendant huit jours avant d'être sauvé en mars 2023. Ses frères de 2 et 5 ans, avait-il témoigné, étaient morts après que leurs parents leur avaient interdit de boire et de manger, sur ordre du gourou. Si M. Wanje espérait la peine capitale pour celui-ci, « au moins les victimes ont-elles obtenu quelque chose », se console-t-il. L'avocat de la défense Lawrence Obonyo a de son côté indiqué à l'AFP que ses clients allaient faire appel, décriant un jugement « pour satisfaire le public ». M. Mackenzie, qui fait également face dans des affaires distinctes à des accusations d' »homicide involontaire » et de « terrorisme », avait « dirigé » la pratique de jeûnes selon une « hiérarchie de la mort », d'après les témoignages : les enfants d'abord, puis les adolescents, les femmes ensuite, et enfin les hommes. Lors du procès, les témoins ont décrit un mouvement qui dénonçait l'enseignement formel comme « satanique », considérait la médecine moderne et les hôpitaux comme des instruments du diable, et exigeait de ses adeptes qu'ils se retirent du monde dans un ranch de Shakahola, une vaste zone de « bush » de la côte kényane. Le gourou avait été arrêté en avril 2023, après que certains fidèles avaient été secourus lorsqu'un groupe de défense des droits humains avait alerté les autorités. L'opération policière avait mis au jour des fosses communes. Une pause dans les fouilles avait dû être décrétée lorsque les morgues locales s'étaient retrouvées débordées par la quantité de corps retrouvés. La Commission nationale kényane pour les droits humains a estimé en 2024 le bilan à 429 morts, dont certains n'ont toujours pas été identifiés. En janvier, M. Mackenzie a été à nouveau mis en accusation après la découverte de 52 autres corps dans un village voisin. Le gourou avait établi « the Good News International Church » (« l'Église internationale de la bonne nouvelle ») en 2003, ouvrant des antennes à Nairobi et le long de la côte kényane, qui ont attiré des milliers de disciples avant qu'il ne décrète leur fermeture en 2019. Beaucoup de Kényans ont demandé des réglementations plus contraignantes, mais sans résultat, pour encadrer les organisations religieuses, notamment après qu'il est apparu que Paul Mackenzie avait été arrêté à deux reprises par le passé, puis relâché. AFP L’article Kenya : 200 ans de prison pour le gourou d'une secte qui affamait ses fidèles pour « rencontrer Jésus » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Fani-Kayode disowns purported conferment of SCN rank
items.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Ambassador Femi Fani-Kayode, has disassociated himself from the purported conferment of the Senior Counsel of Nigeria (SCN) rank, also known as Blue Silk, on him by the Nigerian Law Society (NLS). Fani-Kayode said he neither authorised nor personally approved the acceptance of the designation, describing the circumstances surrounding the conferment as an unfortunate administrative misjudgment. In a statement issued on Friday by his Special Assistant on Media, Lizzy Okoji, the former Minister of Aviation said his representation at the event by members of his staff followed an invitation sent to his office by the society as part of his official engagements. He, however, clarified that neither his staff’s attendance nor any communication subsequently made on his behalf should be interpreted as his personal endorsement or acceptance of the designation. The statement said the circumstances surrounding the representation and the subsequent communication of acceptance were regrettable and occurred without any intention to misrepresent his personal position or professional convictions. Fani-Kayode also raised concerns about the legal and professional implications of the purported conferment, particularly in relation to the statutory framework regulating the legal profession in Nigeria and relevant judicial pronouncements on the conferment of professional ranks outside the established legal framework. Describing himself as a legal practitioner of more than 41 years, he said he would not knowingly engage in any conduct that violates the law, undermines the integrity of the legal profession or brings it into disrepute. He added that he belonged to a family with three generations of legal practitioners and remained committed to upholding the law, professional ethics and the established traditions of the legal profession. The envoy said his clarification was intended to put his position on record, dispel misconceptions arising from the incident and reaffirm his commitment to the rule of law and the dignity of the legal profession. items.title: President Mahama hints at multi-day celebrations for Ghana’s 70th independence anniversary
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has mentioned that Ghana’s 70th Independence Anniversary celebrations in 2027 will span several days. In a recent press briefing, he said the anniversary celebration will have several world leaders in attendance to mark the historic milestone. He noted that Ghana’s status as the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule has generated international interest, with several world leaders expressing a desire to participate in the celebrations. “The 70th anniversary is a very important event, and we’ve started planning towards it. Many world leaders have expressed a wish to come because of Ghana’s prominence as the first to break away from colonialism. So, we expect a lot of heads of state to join us for the celebration,” he said. President Mahama noted that the anniversary planning committee is yet to present its report on the proposed format of the celebrations. However, he indicated that activities would extend beyond 6 March 2027. “It’s not just going to be a day’s event. I’m sure it will be a celebration over a period, with many activities leading up to the event and even after it,” he further indicated. The programme is expected to feature cultural activities and exhibitions showcasing Ghana’s journey since independence, including its achievements and setbacks. “We’ve had our setbacks, but we’ve also had successes, and so we need to showcase all that,” he added. As part of preparations, the President also outlined plans to improve the appearance of Accra and other regional capitals through road rehabilitation, landscaping and other urban renewal works. He said ongoing works in Accra include road repairs and re-marking, fixing damaged pavements and landscaping to give the capital a facelift. Similar improvement works are expected in regional capitals, including the rehabilitation of selected road networks to enhance their appearance ahead of the anniversary. Ghana’s 70th Independence Anniversary will mark seven decades since the country gained independence from British colonial rule on 6 March 1957.

items.title: Paraguay : le président Peña annonce sa démission dans la foulée d’une crise bancaire
items.description: Screenshot " data-large-file="https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/IMG_1312.jpeg?fit=1024%2C677&ssl=1" /> Le président conservateur du Paraguay, Santiago Peña, a annoncé jeudi sa démission, dans la foulée d'un scandale bancaire affectant près de 3 millions d'épargnants, qui a dégénéré en crise politique dans ce pays allié des États-Unis. Son vice-président Pedro Alliana, 52 ans, issu du même parti Colorado, paraissait voué à assumer la présidence du pays de 6,5 millions d'habitants. Le Parlement, réuni en session extraordinaire dans l'après-midi, devait auparavant formellement accepter la démission de M. Peña. « J'ai pris la décision de présenter ma démission de la présidence de la République », a annoncé M. Peña, au pouvoir depuis 2023, dans une vidéo sur X. « Je le fais en pensant à la stabilité de notre pays, à la paix sociale et à la nécessité de préserver nos institutions démocratiques. » L'annonce intervient 48 heures après l'éclatement d'une crise bancaire, qui a vu la Banque centrale du Paraguay (BCP) mettre sous tutelle Ueno Bank, entité financière revendiquant 2,94 millions de clients, dont les dépôts ont été gelés temporairement. – Procès, ou démission – M. Peña avait jusqu'à l'an dernier des actions dans une holding détenant cette banque, à la croissance rapide ces dernières années. La crise de Ueno a déclenché la colère de petits épargnants, qui mardi ont fait le siège à Asuncion d'agences de la banque. Puis ont de nouveau manifesté mercredi soir aux abords du Parlement, où des centaines de personnes ont réclamé la démission de M. Peña aux cris de « Santi fuera ! » (Santi dehors), donnant lieux a des heurts avec la police. « Ueno nous avait approuvé un prêt pour notre première maison. Mais ils n'ont jamais versé l'argent, maintenant nous n'avons plus où vivre », se lamentait auprès de l'AFP Nadia González, 26 ans, mère de trois enfants. Au moment de l'annonce de M. Peña, les députés débattaient en session extraordinaire sa procédure de destitution, finalement approuvée à l'unanimité, y compris le groupe du Parti Colorado du président. Mais ils ont rejeté une procédure de destitution pour le vice-président Alliana, qui lui aussi était visé dans le cadre du scandale Ueno. Ouvrant ainsi la voie à ce qu'il assume la vice-présidence. Des policiers antiémeutes montent la garde devant le Congrès national, réuni en session extraordinaire pour statuer sur une éventuelle procédure de destitution du président Santiago Peña, le 5 novembre 2026 à Asuncion, au Paraguay " width="768" height="511" data-src="/resizer/v2/S5VKD3X55FFF3BW6V4SEHXNP7I.png?auth=f7de7396ae782d9e1067448e39a726cad814c6091c7a6c8532a5212a19f451ed" data-srcset="https://www.dhnet.be/resizer/v2/3TUQN4JXRVGYXKVKFZEYNN2FUA.jpg?auth=eeb7f43b9a4faa9ae4aeb31b7d9a25e9e0089a2f7000c086a01dc572124844ac&width=768&height=511&quality=85&focal=384%2C255 768w" data-sizes="auto" data-optimumx="1" /> Restait toutefois à ce que le Parlement vote jeudi soir pour accepter la démission de Santiago Peña. Une acceptation, synonyme d'impunité, qui faisait débat. Car si la démission est acceptée, M. Peña « conserve son immunité en acquérant le statut de sénateur à vie », expliquait à l'AFP le constitutionnaliste Alcibiades González Delvalle. Et évite un procès en destitution, que mènerait le Sénat. « Je sais qu'il (Santiago Peña) a perdu la légitimité pour gouverner. Je sais que le président, malheureusement, ne sera plus capable de construire des consensus pour poursuivre son gouvernement. Et oui, je sais qu'il est politiquement responsable de ce qui s'est passé », avait déclaré Alejandro Aguilar, un député du Colorado, plaidant pour un procès. Des policiers montent la garde devant une agence de la banque Ueno, à Asuncion, le 3 novembre 2026 au Paraguay " width="768" height="510" data-src="/resizer/v2/S5VKD3X55FFF3BW6V4SEHXNP7I.png?auth=f7de7396ae782d9e1067448e39a726cad814c6091c7a6c8532a5212a19f451ed" data-srcset="https://www.dhnet.be/resizer/v2/W7MP6MJ3AFDQPM4QLWOUVD3LQE.jpg?auth=5000588caaa6357057984edee9c79bdcd33e46a992dd2d9de88280a73da84f21&width=768&height=510&quality=85&focal=384%2C255 768w" data-sizes="auto" data-optimumx="1" /> Dans la foulée de la mise sous tutelle d'Ueno, le président de la BCP, Carlos Carvallo, qui a par le passé dirigé cette même entité, avait annoncé sa démission, réclamée par le président Peña. Huit cadres d'Ueno ont été placés en détention provisoire, et des poursuites ont été engagées contre une vingtaine d'autres personnes depuis mardi. Mercredi, le Parlement a adopté une loi expresse prévoyant de premiers versements, « dès les prochaines 24 heures », à des épargnants lésés, des avances qui pourront atteindre jusqu'à l'équivalent de « 40 salaires mensuels minimum », selon la loi publiée mercredi par le chef de l'État sur X, soit 121 millions de guaranis (près de 20.000 dollars). – « Sans argent » – « Je n'ai même pas envie de parler, ce n'est même pas la peine parce qu'aujourd'hui je suis sans argent. Maintenant, il faut attendre 4 heures pour qu'on nous assigne une banque où nous irons récupérer le fruit de nos efforts », grondait Reinaldo Gómez, 48 ans, vendeur ambulant dans le centre d'Asunción. Dans son message de démission, Santiago Peña affirmait n'avoir désormais « qu'une priorité : la tranquillité des Paraguayens qui ont confié leurs économies à notre système financier ». « Je veux demander pardon au peuple si, à un moment donné, j'ai failli. Je n'ai jamais eu l'intention de trahir la confiance que vous aviez placée en moi », a-t-il ajouté. Santiago Peña avait été élu confortablement en 2023. Cet économiste, passé notamment par la BCP et le Fonds monétaire international, incarnait la jeune génération du Parti Colorado, hégémonique depuis sept décennies sur la politique paraguayenne. AFP L’article Paraguay : le président Peña annonce sa démission dans la foulée d'une crise bancaire est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Have you set a Christmas budget, or are you leaving it to chance?
items.description: The countdown to Christmas has started, and so has the spending headache. How do you make the season feel special without emptying your pocket? As the festive season approaches, one question is already splitting people: how much are you planning to spend? For many households, Christmas is no longer just about celebration. It is about food, new clothes, transport, gifts, church offerings, and outings, all landing in the same month, at a time when prices are already high. Some are planning early to avoid the last-minute rush. Others say there is simply nothing to plan with. For some, the answer is already in thousands. For others, there is no budget at all, just hope, and whatever comes. Alberta said she is ready to go all out this year, because after a difficult year, she wants to give back to the people who stood by her. “My budget is about two thousand cedis or three thousand for the Christmas and even maybe more than that if things go right because this Christmas must be great. I have a lot of things I have to give to people. My mom, some of my friends that really made the year really good to me.” For her, Christmas is not about showing off. It is about appreciation. The people who made the year bearable deserve to be remembered, even if it means stretching the budget a little further than planned. Ms Patricia is taking the opposite approach, no plan, no pressure. “This Christmas I don’t really have a budget. If anything goes well, fine. If it doesn’t, fine. If I had money like maybe I’ll try and then get myself a new phone or something but I don’t have money, I’ll wait for people to send me Christmas gifts. What will happen should happen.” It is a feeling many can relate to. When money is tight, Christmas becomes less about what you will buy, and more about what will come your way. There is no new phone, no big shopping, just waiting, and hoping someone remembers you. Then there is the detailed planner, Mr. Ben, the one who has already broken Christmas down line by line, cedi by cedi, so nothing catches him by surprise. “You all know it’s Christmas. You have to look good. You have to look nice. So I might get my hair, my clothes. Yes, I’m wearing new clothes. So I’ll put three hundred cedis for that.” “Then Christmas you have to show love to your friends and family. So you have to gift. So for gifts I’ll put some small two hundred cedis here.” “Then outings with friends. You have to go to parties with friends to make the Christmas more fun. So you have to put some 250 cedis for outings.” “And from after the outing, you know Christmas, you have to go and give thanks to God. So you have to go to the house of the Lord and give offerings too.” “That’s my plan for Christmas. I don’t know about yours. Merry Christmas to everyone in advance.” His plan captures what Christmas means for many, looking good, showing love, having fun, and giving thanks. Even with just GH¢1000 for clothes, gifts and outings, plus an offering, he has found a way to make the season feel complete without trying to do everything at once. And that is really the heart of the Christmas money talk. It is not about who spends the most. It is about knowing what matters to you, and finding a way to celebrate it without starting the new year broke. So, what have you decided? Are you a planner, a giver, or are you going with the flow?

items.title: SIPSIS 2026 : plus de 5 000 participants attendus à Ouagadougou
items.description: La deuxième édition du Salon international des professionnels de santé et de l’intégration des soins (SIPSIS) se tiendra du 25 au 28 novembre 2026 à la salle de conférence de Ouaga 2000. Prévu pour réunir plus de 5 000 participants issus d’une dizaine de pays, ce rendez-vous entend mobiliser les acteurs de l’écosystème sanitaire autour des défis de la décennie 2027-2036. L’annonce a été faite le 6 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, lors d’une conférence de presse. Placée sous le thème « Défis sanitaires de la décennie 2027-2036 en Afrique : perspectives stratégiques pour la Confédération des États du Sahel dans le contexte de la souveraineté », cette deuxième édition ambitionne de dégager des priorités communes. Elle vise également à faire émerger des projets et des partenariats capables de renforcer les capacités locales et la coopération entre les acteurs. Le Mali et le Niger sont les deux pays invités d’honneur de cette édition. « La souveraineté sanitaire exige de mobiliser un écosystème plus large que le secteur classique », a souligné le directeur de cabinet du ministre de la Santé, Adjima Combary. Pour les organisateurs, la réponse aux défis sanitaires ne relève pas uniquement des professionnels de santé. Elle nécessite également l’implication de secteurs comme l’agriculture, l’eau, l’alimentation, l’environnement, l’éducation, l’énergie, le numérique, la recherche et l’industrie. Six composantes pour mobiliser les acteurs de l’écosystème sanitaire Le programme s’articulera autour de six grandes composantes. Il comprend des activités scientifiques, des expositions, des rencontres professionnelles B2B, un espace « SIPSIS et jeunesse », des visites de terrain ainsi que la Nuit de l’écosystème de santé. Des visites du Centre hospitalier universitaire de Pala et du barrage de Samandéni sont également annoncées. Les organisateurs attendent plus de 5 000 participants issus d’une dizaine de pays, 100 exposants et plus de 100 communications scientifiques. Une cinquantaine de rendez-vous d’affaires (B2B) et plus de 50 partenariats sont également annoncés. Le salon entend par ailleurs accorder une place à la formation et à la relève. Un manuel de découverte des métiers de l’écosystème de la santé est prévu pour accompagner l’orientation des jeunes et leur faire découvrir la diversité des professions qui contribuent à la santé des populations. Lancé en 2024, le SIPSIS se veut un cadre de concertation entre les institutions, les professionnels, les entreprises et les organisations intervenant dans l’écosystème sanitaire. Cette deuxième édition entend ainsi consolider les synergies entre les différents secteurs pour mieux répondre aux besoins des populations. Des retombées attendues au Burkina Faso, dans l’AES et en Afrique Pour le Burkina Faso, les retombées attendues portent notamment sur la valorisation des compétences et des capacités nationales. L’accueil des délégations pourrait également contribuer à dynamiser certains secteurs économiques. À l’échelle de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES), les échanges devraient favoriser l’identification de priorités communes et de complémentarités entre les pays. Ils pourraient également ouvrir la voie à des projets conjoints, notamment dans la production et l’approvisionnement en produits de santé. Pour l’Afrique, les organisateurs ambitionnent de renforcer la circulation des connaissances, la visibilité des innovations et des savoirs thérapeutiques africains. Le rapprochement entre institutions, entreprises et chercheurs devrait également favoriser les transferts de compétences et l’émergence de solutions adaptées aux besoins des populations. Les travaux devront aboutir à la Déclaration de Ouagadougou 2026. Ce document servira de cadre de recommandations pour consolider les orientations issues des échanges et éclairer les priorités sanitaires de la décennie 2027-2036. « Les échanges doivent favoriser l’émergence de projets conjoints », a indiqué Adjima Combary, appelant les départements ministériels, les institutions, les professionnels et les entreprises à apporter une contribution concrète à cette dynamique. Les modalités de participation au SIPSIS 2026 sont disponibles sur la plateforme officielle du salon www.sipsis.bf . Éléonore Savadogo Faso7 L’article SIPSIS 2026 : plus de 5 000 participants attendus à Ouagadougou est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Russia’s expanding media partnerships in Africa: Opportunities, risks and the imperative of media independence
items.description: Russia’s expanding media engagement in Africa was evident at the October 2026 Russia–Africa Media Forum in Moscow, where organisers reported the signing of 29 media cooperation documents involving Russian and African institutions. RT alone announced agreements with 12 African media organisations and ministries, while TASS and Rossiya Segodnya concluded additional arrangements covering news exchange, broadcasting cooperation and professional development. For African media organisations, these partnerships potentially offer opportunities for professional development, technical cooperation and greater diversity in international news coverage. However, amid growing concerns about Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI), they also raise questions about editorial independence, transparency and democratic governance. Beyond these concerns lies an important question: What gaps are these partnerships filling, and why are African media organisations increasingly looking to new international partners to address their needs? Russia’s growing media partnerships The October 2026 forum brought together more than 200 participants from 46 African countries. According to RT, cooperation agreements involved media institutions in Nigeria, Tanzania, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Ethiopia and several other African countries. Ghana’s participation is particularly significant. On 26 October 2026, the Ghana Broadcasting Corporation (GBC) announced a cooperation agreement with Rossiya Segodnya, Russia’s state-owned international information agency. According to GBC’s official report, the agreement provides for English-language news exchange, assistance to journalists, joint media activities and possible professional training. GBC’s Director-General, Professor Amin Alhassan, indicated that the partnership would contribute to more balanced coverage of Russia. Similarly, Nigeria’s TVC Communications signed an agreement with RT covering content exchange and professional cooperation. These arrangements may broaden the international perspectives available to African audiences, particularly where international news coverage has traditionally depended heavily on Western sources. Nevertheless, their benefits will depend on implementation and the ability of participating institutions to maintain independent editorial judgement. What gaps are these partnerships filling? The attraction of such partnerships cannot be separated from the economic and institutional challenges confronting African journalism. Across the continent, media organisations face declining advertising revenues, rising operational costs, technological disruption and inadequate resources for investigative reporting and professional development. In Ghana, The State of the Ghanaian Media Report (2023), produced by the Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA) in collaboration with the University of Ghana, highlights persistent financial sustainability challenges, poor remuneration and job insecurity. With many media organisations struggling to break even, these vulnerabilities increase the appeal of external partnerships offering technical and professional support. The Global Forum for Media Development’s 2026 assessment of media assistance in sub-Saharan Africa further identified uneven funding distribution and limited flexible institutional support. Such findings suggest that existing assistance models do not sufficiently address the long-term sustainability needs of African media. Reductions in international development assistance, particularly following changes to United States foreign assistance in 2025, have further exposed the vulnerability of externally dependent media institutions. Against this background, partnerships offering news content, professional training and international distribution networks become understandably attractive. Russia’s engagement can therefore be understood partly as responding to identifiable needs within African media markets. It must be noted, however, that the agreements do not necessarily establish that Russia is providing substantial financial assistance or addressing the underlying sustainability challenges. Foreign information manipulation: The other side of the partnership While international media cooperation offers legitimate benefits, it can also create vulnerabilities when foreign partnerships become channels for political influence or coordinated information manipulation. Foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI) generally involves intentional, coordinated and often deceptive activities intended to manipulate information environments or influence political and democratic processes. It is important to note that legitimate international broadcasting, public diplomacy or opinions favourable to a particular country should not automatically be classified as FIMI. Recent findings by Meta illustrate why this distinction matters. In its first-half 2026 threat reporting, Meta disclosed that it had disrupted a coordinated inauthentic behaviour network originating in Russia and targeting audiences in Ghana, Angola, Kenya and South Africa. The operation involved 37 Facebook accounts and 29 Pages, with approximately 30,000 followers across the Pages. According to Meta, the network used apparently local news sources and online identities to amplify anti-Western narratives and portray Russia as an alternative international partner. Interestingly, the operation did not rely exclusively on fabricated information. It also circulated authentic news articles and commentary, sometimes using fictitious identities or falsely attributed bylines. These findings demonstrate that information manipulation can involve selective presentation and artificial amplification of genuine information, not merely the publication of falsehoods. For Ghana and other African democracies, such operations raise concerns about the potential manipulation of public opinion and erosion of trust in democratic institutions. These concerns are particularly relevant in the Sahel, where competing narratives about military governance, sovereignty and constitutional democracy circulate across national borders. However, Meta’s findings do not establish that GBC or other African institutions participating in the October agreements were involved in the identified operation. Conflating legitimate media partnerships with documented covert influence campaigns would be misleading. The lesson is therefore not that cooperation with Russian media necessarily constitutes FIMI, but that foreign media partnerships require transparency and appropriate editorial safeguards. Western partners must rethink their approach Russia’s growing media engagement also presents an opportunity for reflection among traditional media development partners. European and North American governments, development agencies and philanthropic organisations have contributed significantly to African journalism through investments in investigative reporting, journalist safety, media freedom and institutional development. These contributions remain important. However, prevailing funding arrangements, often characterised by short-term projects and limited institutional financing, do not always address the long-term sustainability needs of African media organisations. Western partners should therefore consider greater investment in predictable, multi-year institutional support, digital infrastructure, newsroom sustainability and locally determined professional development priorities. Such support should also be more accessible to African-led organisations rather than disproportionately channelled through international intermediaries. Importantly, this should not become a geopolitical competition to prevent African media organisations from cooperating with Russia. Instead, Western partners should become more responsive and equitable partners, strengthening the capacity of African media institutions to operate independently regardless of their international relationships. Beyond Russia and the West: African ownership and sustainability Perhaps the most important lesson is that African media organisations cannot continue relying indefinitely on external partners for their institutional survival. Whether support comes from Russia, Europe, North America, China or elsewhere, international cooperation is rarely entirely detached from the interests and priorities of those providing it. Western assistance may sometimes reflect governance approaches or social and cultural perspectives that do not fully align with local contexts. Similarly, Russian and other state-linked partnerships may advance geopolitical narratives or foreign policy interests. This does not mean internationally recognised principles of media freedom, human rights and professional journalism should be compromised. Rather, African media institutions must retain the independence to determine their editorial priorities and institutional development needs. Dependence on external assistance also exposes media organisations to changing donor priorities, political transitions and sudden funding withdrawals. The longer-term response must therefore involve greater African investment in journalism. Governments should strengthen transparent financing mechanisms for public service broadcasting while protecting editorial independence. Media owners must invest in viable business models and technological innovation. African businesses and philanthropic institutions should increasingly recognise independent journalism as a public good deserving sustained support. Regional institutions, including ECOWAS and the African Union, could also explore mechanisms for supporting media innovation, investigative journalism and cross-border collaboration, with safeguards against political and commercial interference. The objective should be African-led diversified and sustainable media development partnerships, in which international assistance complements locally determined priorities rather than defining them.

Le texte précise que des commerçants contrevenants ont été réquisitionnés pour exécuter des travaux d’intérêt général. ​Dans le cadre de ses missions de régulation du marché et de protection des consommateurs, la Brigade Mobile de Contrôle économique et de Répression des Fraudes (BMCRF) a mené des sorties inopinées dans plusieurs arrondissements de Ouagadougou. « De Saaba à Wemtenga, en passant par la Patte d'Oie et Nagrin, le maillage a été resserré», lit-on sur la page Facebook de la BMCRF qui souligne que l'opération ciblait en premier lieu le respect des prix conseillés des boissons. «Des dépôts-caves, des débits de boissons ou des maquis, aucun maillon de la chaîne de commercialisation n’a échappé à la vigilance des contrôleurs» qui, face aux abus constatés, ont procédé «purement et simplement à la fermeture de plusieurs maquis et scellé des boutiques indélicates». Par ailleurs, «des stocks de produits périmés, prohibés ont été saisis et retirés des circuits de distribution. Les contrevenants épinglés ont été réquisitionnés pour exécuter des travaux d’intérêt général», déclare la BMCRF qui salue la collaboration des citoyens. Par Wakat Séra L’article Ouagadougou: des commerçants contrevenants réquisitionnés pour des travaux d’intérêt général est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: ‘Stop your rants, go sort your mess’ — APC tackles ADC over court ruling
items.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) has urged the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to resolve its internal leadership crisis instead of accusing the ruling party of colluding with the judiciary over a court judgment nullifying the David Mark-led leadership and the presidential candidacy of Atiku Abubakar. The APC, in a statement issued on Friday by its National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, described the ADC’s reaction to the judgment as “senseless rants” and insisted that the ruling party had no involvement in the legal dispute. Morka said the ADC had repeatedly accused the APC of collusion and attacked the judiciary whenever court decisions went against it, but praised the courts when rulings favoured the opposition party. He accused the ADC of disregarding the independence and authority of the judiciary, arguing that it considered only judges who ruled in its favour to be worthy of respect. “The ADC touts its desire to win power and govern democratic Nigeria without any iota of regard for the authority and independence of the judiciary, an indispensable pillar of any democracy,” he said. The APC spokesman maintained that the case was an internal ADC dispute initiated by party officers against the Mark-led leadership, which he described as an unlawful takeover. “To be clear, APC is neither a party nor an interlocutor in the matter. Nothing about the case has anything to do with the APC,” Morka said. He said the court’s decision followed a legal challenge by ADC national officers who alleged that Mark and other leaders took control of the party in violation of its internal democracy. Morka described the judgment delivered by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja as a demonstration of the independence of the judiciary and the rule of law. The ruling sacked the Mark-led leadership and invalidated decisions taken by the executive, including the party’s primary election processes and outcomes. The APC spokesman advised the ADC to challenge the judgment through the appropriate legal channels if it was dissatisfied with the outcome. “If ADC is dissatisfied with that decision, it should exercise its constitutional right of appeal rather than engage in partisan mudslinging against our great Party and issuing threats to incite anarchy,” he said. Morka further described the ADC as a party unfit to govern Nigeria, arguing that its inability to resolve its internal disputes raised questions about its capacity to manage the country. “A party that cannot fix itself cannot possibly fix Africa’s most important country,” he said. He added that the APC and the Tinubu administration remained committed to democracy, the rule of law and good governance, despite what he called the opposition’s “irresponsible and dangerous rhetoric.” The post ‘Stop your rants, go sort your mess’ — APC tackles ADC over court ruling appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : Kalama, quand les mots deviennent une discipline olympique
items.description: La finale de la compétition Kalama s’est déroulée ce jeudi 5 septembre au théâtre national Daniel Sorano. Au terme de la soirée, Sandrine Zohou, 28 ans, Togolaise, résidant en France s’est illustrée en remportant la médaille d’or. La finale proposée par l’agence française de développement (AFD) et Eloquentia avait pour thème « la parole, discipline olympique « . Le projet « La parole, discipline olympique » a pour objectif de former 10 jeunes à porter le message de la solidarité internationale. Les jeux olympiques de la jeunesse ne sont pas seulement qu’un évènement sportif, c'est aussi un espace d'expression unique où la jeunesse du Sénégal, de la France se rassemble pour porter haut les valeurs de solidarité internationale. C’est ce qu’a compris l’AFD et Eloquentia. Derrière cette soirée se cache une longue sélection. Ils étaient 100 sur la ligne de départ. 50 ont atteint l’étape de la demi-finale. Finalement, ils ne sont plus que 10 à avoir monté la scène du théâtre Sorano. La compétition s'est articulée autour de 5 duels intenses fonctionnant sur le principe du « POUR » ou du « CONTRE ». Les participants ont dû croiser le fer sur des sujets percutants et ancrés dans l'actualité sportive et sociétale sur un chrono entre 5 et 7mns30 : Le sport est-il apolitique ? Faux départ ? Les anneaux ont-ils perdu leurs valeurs ? ? Faut-il enjamber tous les obstacles ? S’engager c’est porter un poids ? Au terme d’une rude bataille d’éloquence Sandrine Zohou, 28 ans, Togolaise, résidant en France qui était « pour », « faux départ » s’est illustrée en remportant à la médaille d’or. A lire aussi : Concours d’éloquence Kalama : Irène Mendy, finaliste sénégalaise, portera la parole olympique à Dakar Elle est suivie par le sénégalais Youssoupha Gueye, Alice Perdriel Vaissière, la benjamine (18 ans) de cette finale occupe la troisième place. Irene Mendy, étudiante en journalisme et l’une des candidates du Sénégal n’a pas pu se retrouver sur le podium mais remporte quand même une médaille olympique et repart avec une expérience enrichissante. Ces finalistes représentent un pont entre les cultures : ils sont 5 jeunes vivant en France et 5 jeunes vivant au Sénégal, âgés de 18 à 28 ans. Ne se connaissant pas il y a encore quelques mois, ils se sont entraînés comme des athlètes pour porter leur voix ensemble. Leurs efforts visaient un seul but : convaincre. Pour Stéphanie Beney, responsable de projet, partenariat avec les organisations de la société civile à l’AFD : « L’AFD est particulièrement engagée au côté du Sénégal dans le cadre des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse à Dakar. Cet engagement s'inscrit dans une coopération plus large entre la France et le Sénégal, portée notamment par le ministère des Affaires étrangères, et l'ambassade de France au Sénégal. L'AFD accompagne également des initiatives d'éducation à la citoyenneté et c'est très important pour nous pour permettre aux jeunes de mieux comprendre le monde et de s'y engager. » De son côté, Laurane Bourgoint, Directrice générale Eloquentia affirme que ces 10 finalistes ne sont pas seulement « des lauréats d'un concours, ils sont désormais des ambassadeurs, des ambassadeurs de jeunesse pour pouvoir s'engager, qui ont des choses à dire et qui entendent bien toute sa place dans les grands rendez-vous de monde. Et je crois que finalement, c'est ça notre plus grande réussite. » Fatou NGOM

items.title: Australia sanctions El Burhan and Hemedti over Sudan war and human rights abuses
items.description: Australia has imposed targeted sanctions, and travel bans on four Sudanese individuals, including Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) Commander and Transitional Sovereignty Council President Lt Gen Abdelfattah El Burhan and paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as ‘Hemedti’, over the ongoing war in Sudan. Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong announced the measures in a statement published by the ministry on Thursday, saying the government had also imposed financial sanctions on the El Bara Bin Malik Brigade . Among those on the sanctions list are Al-Tijani Al-Tahir Karshoum, the RSF-aligned de facto governor of West Darfur, and RSF field commander Hussein Barsham. Both face financial sanctions and travel bans. “The RSF and the SAF have committed serious human rights violations and abuses, including attacks on civilians, torture, sexual and gender-based violence , and extrajudicial killings,” Wong said. “Those responsible for serious human rights violations and abuses must be held to account.” The sanctions build on measures Australia previously imposed on 13 individuals under the United Nations Security Council’s Sudan sanctions framework. Under the new measures, dealing with the assets of listed individuals or the El Baraa Bin Malik Brigade without ministerial authorisation is a criminal offence. The four individuals are also barred from entering or remaining in Australia. Australia said hundreds of thousands of people had been killed and more than 14 million displaced since the war began on 15 April 2023. Almost 34 million people, more than 70 per cent of Sudan’s population, need humanitarian assistance . Canberra has provided more than $67 million in humanitarian aid to Sudan, supporting food, clean water, shelter, healthcare and protection services. To ensure sanctions do not obstruct relief efforts, Wong also issued a humanitarian permit allowing specified aid activities that would otherwise be restricted under the sanctions framework. Share article The post Australia sanctions El Burhan and Hemedti over Sudan war and human rights abuses appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

items.title: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park calls for Independence Declaration photo on selected banknotes
items.description: The Management of the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park has called on the Bank of Ghana (BoG) to replace the image of the Big Six on selected banknote denominations with the historic photograph of Ghana’s independence declaration on March 6, 1957. The proposal is aimed at broadening the historical representation on the country’s currency by recognising other defining moments in Ghana’s history, while preserving the significance of the Big Six in the independence struggle. In a press release issued on Friday, November 6, the Park said the Big Six image currently features on almost all Ghanaian banknotes but argued that the country’s currency should also reflect other important milestones in its history. It maintained that banknotes are more than a medium of exchange, describing them as important symbols of national identity, heritage, pride and collective memory. The Management is therefore proposing that the iconic photograph capturing Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah declaring Ghana’s independence be featured on selected denominations. It said the proposal is consistent with the Bank of Ghana’s planned introduction of a Heritage Series of banknotes, which would provide an opportunity to celebrate significant personalities, events and milestones in the country’s national history. According to the Park, the photograph captures the culmination of Ghana’s independence struggle and the historic moment the country broke free from colonial rule. It described the event as a defining turning point in Ghana’s history and a landmark in the wider African liberation struggle, representing the country’s freedom, sovereignty and national identity. The Management believes featuring the photograph on selected banknotes would be particularly significant as Ghana prepares to mark the 70th anniversary of its independence in 2027. It said the move would serve as a fitting and enduring tribute to the historic moment that gave birth to the nation.
